06_marg110: RABANUS. The barley meal signifies the knowledge of the old law, which is well compared to barley, because as barley, cleansed from the chaff with great labour, is brought to meal, so the letter of the law, ground by the millstone of discernment, gives forth the meal of the spiritual sense; and rightly the tenth part of a measure is offered, because the law consists of ten commandments, of which any commandment is a tenth part, against which the wicked wife is said to have acted. The woman therefore is offered to the priest with the oblation of the tenth part when she is reserved for the judgment of Christ, according to the law divinely given, to be condemned or freed.
06_interl131: of flattery or of indiscreet mercy
06_marg111: RABANUS. etc. It is not fitting that the impenitent be anointed with the oil of flattery or of indiscreet mercy, nor with the frankincense of superfluous praise or of disordered prayer; but that vice be pursued earnestly and in order with the zeal of justice according to the Lord's precept.
06_interl132: because she is kept to be judged by divine judgment
06_interl133: the divine wisdom, namely, contained in the lowly letter of the Law
06_marg112: To this water the priest mixes a little earth from the pavement of the tabernacle, when by the decree of Christ the remembrance of the patriarchs, prophets and apostles is found brought in.
06_marg113: AND THE PRIEST SHALL WRITE etc. Because, namely, the punishment of sinners is set out in holy Scripture. And whoever drinks it piously and faithfully, dreading the punishments of sinners which are told in it and abstaining from sins, for him the most bitter water will become salvation. But he who despises it, his belly swelling, his thigh shall rot, and he shall be a curse and an example, because he will be punished by the just judgment of God, and his desires and acts will be to him a reproach.
06_marg114: AND HE SHALL GIVE HER TO DRINK: that her sin may be made manifest, either here for correction or in the future for damnation. For there is nothing hidden that shall not be revealed. Hence the Lord says: The word that I have spoken, the same shall judge you in the last day.
06_interl136: This is done when the confession of the holy Trinity is found in the sacrifice of the Law, which is worthily offered on the altar of faith.
06_interl144: by falling back into the pleasure of past vice
06_interl145: lest they grow pale with abstinence for vainglory
06_marg115: AND THE LORD SPOKE etc. FROM WINE AND FROM EVERY etc. ISIDORE. In the twelfth station, that is, Sinai, the Nazarites are commanded not to drink or eat wine and strong drink and everything that can make drunk. In the Proverbs too it is commanded that the mighty and the wrathful drink no wine, lest they forget wisdom. In the Nazarites the life of the continent is marked; to them wine is forbidden, that is, wantonness; and strong drink, that is, every earthly pleasure. For strong drink is made from diverse kinds, as pleasure from the diverse passion of vices. For those do not drink wine but drink strong drink who, to deceive men, feign certain shadows and images of virtues. They eat dried grapes who stain themselves with the pallor of abstinence before human eyes, that they may take glory from men. They drink vinegar who after holiness of life slip back into the oldness of past vices and delight in the corruption of the old wickedness.
06_marg116: That is: he shall keep neither guile nor malice in his mind, lest, namely, the hair of the head, that is, the thought of the mind, be defiled; but let him keep innocence to the end of life. For otherwise the vow will not be acceptable. But he that shall persevere shall be saved.
06_marg117: That is: he shall not imitate one dead in sins, nor enter the way of his iniquity, lest he lose his labour. For not he who begins, but he who finishes, shall be crowned.
06_marg118: That is: let no carnal affection draw him back; every person, every dignity, every kinship is to be set after the service of Christ.
06_marg119: That is: the grace of the Holy Ghost is poured forth in his heart. Whence: Grieve not the Holy Spirit of God, whereby you are all sealed.
06_marg120: That is: let him persevere to the end without the defilement of sin and trespass.
06_marg121: That is: if he has wished to imitate one defiled by mortal sin, and has gone down as far as consent, let him know that his continence must needs be defiled and his head shaved, that is, his mind cleansed from wicked thought and harmful delight.
06_marg122: In the time, namely, of compunction, when he knows he has offended, let him strive at once to amend himself, and always fear a like fall.
06_interl147: by which the time of the resurrection is signified
06_marg123: The turtles signify chastity, the young pigeons simplicity. He therefore who wishes to come to the resurrection of the good, let him offer to the true priest, that is, Christ, chastity of mind and body, and simplicity in the catholic faith, through which he enters the Church, that he may be expiated through the help of so great a high priest.
06_interl148: he will make him groan, namely, for sins through fear of hell
06_interl149: that he may sigh, namely, with desire of eternal life
06_marg124: Our advocate with the Father. Or because he will make us pray, according to that: "The Spirit asketh for us with unspeakable groanings."
06_interl150: the mind rescued from carnal desire
06_interl151: that all may be holy and spotless
06_interl152: an innocent life for a criminal one, simplicity for craftiness
06_marg125: Let him presume nothing of his former conversation, but trust in the grace of God alone, by whose gift he receives pardon and everlasting rest.
06_marg126: When the just man shall turn himself away from his justice and do iniquity, all his justices shall be forgotten.
06_marg127: THIS IS THE LAW etc. After the lawgiver has instructed the Nazarite how he is to be cleansed if his consecration is defiled by the dead, he adds how, after the vow is completed, he should present himself to the Lord with an oblation to give thanks; mystically hinting that the life of the continent, with the oblation of work and cleanness of heart, will please the Lord in a good end.
06_marg128: He offers this who puts all his hope in his immolation, of whom it is said: Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who taketh away the sins of the world. He offers him for a holocaust when for his love, by mortifying the flesh, he consecrates to the Lord his whole life kindled with the ardour of charity.
06_marg129: Another reading: And he shall offer his gift to the Lord, a lamb of a year without blemish for holocausts, and one ewe lamb of a year without blemish "into sin". This some would not translate, as though avoiding an unusual expression, and said "for sin", not "into sin", although the sense in that expression is not to be disturbed. For "into sin" was said because what was offered for sin was called sin. Whence: Him that knew no sin, for us he hath made sin, that is, a sacrifice for sin. As therefore the lamb "into holocaust", so also the ewe lamb "into sin", so that the animal itself was sin, that is, a sacrifice for sin; as of the ram, which follows, he says "into saving", which he makes plain afterward by repeating. For he also says "for sin" what he had said before "into sin"; and "this sacrifice of saving" what he had said before "into saving".
06_marg130: Tropologically. He offers a lamb for a holocaust who shows God simplicity of heart with the devotion of charity; a ewe, who shows an example of innocence; and a ram as a peace victim, when he rules himself well in the way of God and subjects the rebellious flesh to the command of the soul.
06_marg131: He offers a ewe for sin who faithfully believes that Christ, the innocent, was offered for the sin of the human race.
06_marg132: This is done when he trusts that he is the one who by the dispensation of the flesh made peace between things heavenly and earthly, emptying every principality and power: whom "God hath exalted, and hath given him a name which is above every name" etc.
06_interl157: of gladness, the grace of the Holy Ghost
06_marg133: The old law, dictated by the Holy Ghost and tempered for human profit.
06_marg134: Without leaven: because spiritual grace lies open in the law and in the Gospel to those who understand rightly.
06_marg135: Presenting the merit and labour of each, his meditation and observance of the law, in the sight of God by rewarding it, at the entrance of the heavenly life, the contest of good work being finished.
06_marg136: BUT THE RAM etc. Showing him, namely, worthy of the reward of everlasting rest, as the prince and best leader of himself or of others, who has ruled and led himself well in the path of God's commandments, according to the doctrine of the Scriptures and the grace of the spiritual gifts.
06_interl160: the mind, namely, of one abstaining from superfluous thoughts
06_marg137: What is it that the Nazarites grow their hair, except that through a life of great continence the thoughts of presumption grow? But what is it that, the devotion being completed, the Nazarite is commanded to shave his head and put the hair in the fire of the sacrifice, except that we then reach the height of perfection when we so conquer outward vices that we also cut off superfluous thoughts from the mind? To burn these in the fire of the sacrifice is to kindle them with the flame of divine love, so that the whole heart burns in the love of God, and, burning up superfluous thoughts, consumes as it were the hair of the Nazarite by the perfection of devotion.
06_interl163: by revealing the obscure mysteries of the Scriptures
06_marg138: The strength, namely, of work, boiled and proved in the fire of tribulation, the high priest makes his holy one offer to God the Father.
06_marg139: AND ONE WAFER: helping him, namely, by the gift of the Holy Ghost to complete in work the knowledge of the law.
06_interl165: that is: when he has stripped him of the corruption of the flesh and freed him from the burden of cares.
06_marg140: HE SHALL ELEVATE: he will present to the Father, namely, the good things which the continent man has wrought, and will have them rewarded with everlasting reward.
06_marg141: SHALL BELONG TO THE PRIEST: because whatever the Nazarite has willed well and completed in deed pertains to his glory. For he it is who worketh in us both to will and to accomplish.
06_interl167: because our wisdom is his own gift
06_marg142: That is: after right intention, discreet promise, perfection of work, retribution of reward.
06_marg143: DRINK WINE: to drink in the spiritual gift fully and freely; whence: "Thou shalt make them drink of the torrent of thy pleasure."
06_interl172: which, namely, he will do of his own accord
06_marg144: AND THE LORD SPOKE etc. Moses signifies the law, Aaron the priesthood, and his sons the order of the Church. The Lord therefore teaches through the law the order of priests how they should build up the people by preaching and strengthen them by frequent prayer and blessing.
06_marg145: Moses has a manifold signification. He bears the figure of the Jewish people when he holds the serpent's tail; for it signifies that the Jews will come to the faith of Christ at the end of the world. He signifies the law also, as we showed above. He bears the person of Christ, who frees his elect from the spiritual Egypt through the water of baptism, when he leads the people out of Egypt through the Red Sea, when he completes, sets up and anoints the tabernacle.
06_interl173: by the pouring in of the spiritual gifts
06_interl174: whose it is to keep; whence: "Unless the Lord keep the city, he watcheth in vain that keepeth it."
06_marg146: It is to be noted that in this blessing the name of the Lord is brought in three times, that the holy Trinity may be understood, from whom and through whom and in whom all good things are to be sought and obtained, because of him and by him and in him are all things.
06_marg147: May he keep by his grace the blessing which you have received. "Unless the Lord keep the city, he watcheth in vain that keepeth it."
06_marg148: The showing of God's face is propitiation, and the showing of true salvation; whence: "Shew us thy face, and we shall be saved."
06_marg149: TURN etc. The turning of the face signifies mercy, the turning away, wrath. Whence: "Look thou upon me, and have mercy on me." And elsewhere: Why turnest thou thy face away, and forgettest our want? We must pray therefore that he whose help we turn away from us by sinning would deign, by his goodness, to make his face shine upon us, that, rescuing us from our enemies, he may grant everlasting peace.
06_marg150: It is the priests' part to invoke the name of the Lord; the Lord's to accomplish what is asked. Let no one therefore ascribe to himself what the Trinity alone grants to whom it will.
